title: Baked pasta shells with ricotta and spinach
description: Big pasta shells filled with ricotta, spinach and parmesan, baked in tomato sauce under béchamel and mozzarella. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a pan with a splash of water, cool it, squeeze it very dry and chop it. Mix with the ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, the nutmeg and half the salt.
steps.tip: Squeeze the spinach hard, or the filling goes watery.

steps: Simmer the passata with the oil, crushed garlic and the rest of the salt for 10 minutes.

steps.text: Cook the shells in salted water for 3 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and lay them out on a tray so they do not stick.
steps.tip: They finish cooking in the oven, so keep them firm.

steps: Make a béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 4 minutes until thick.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Spread the tomato sauce in a baking dish, fill each shell with a spoon of filling and sit them in the sauce.

steps.text: Spoon the béchamel over, scatter with torn mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan and bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
steps.tip: It can be assembled a day ahead and baked when you need it.

title: Small pasta with lentils
description: Brown lentils simmered with onion, carrot, celery, garlic and bay into a thick soup, with small pasta cooked in at the end. Cheap and filling. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Chop the onion, carrot and celeriac very finely.

steps.text: Soften them in {4 tbsp} of the oil in a deep pot on low for 10 minutes, add the garlic and bay leaves for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Slowly softened vegetables are the flavour base here, so take your time.

steps.text: Add the rinsed lentils and {1500 ml} water and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are almost soft.
steps.tip: Salt now, not at the start, so the lentils soften well.

steps.text: Add the salt, chili and pasta and cook, stirring often, until the pasta is soft, about 10 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
steps.tip: It should be a thick soup you can almost eat with a fork.

steps: Serve with a drizzle of the rest of the oil and grated parmesan.

title: Pasta with creamy pumpkin, garlic and chili
description: Pumpkin cooked down in olive oil and butter with garlic and chili into a silky purée that clings to small pasta. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.

steps.text: Peel the pumpkin (Hokkaido can keep its skin) and cut it into small cubes.
steps.tip: Small cubes cook faster and break down into a smoother sauce.

steps.text: Warm the oil, butter, chopped garlic and chili in a wide pan, add the pumpkin and salt, cover and cook on medium-low for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until it collapses into a purée.
steps.tip: Add a splash of water if it starts to stick.

steps: Meanwhile cook the pasta in salted water until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Toss the pasta with the pumpkin, adding pasta water a little at a time until silky. Stir in the parsley.
steps.tip: The starchy water is what turns the purée into a sauce.

steps: Serve with grated parmesan and a pinch more chili.

title: Farfalle with smoked salmon, mascarpone and lemon
description: A no-cook sauce of smoked salmon, mascarpone, butter and lemon peel, loosened with pasta water and finished with dill. Ready in 15 minutes. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil.

steps.text: Cut the salmon into strips. In a big serving bowl, mix it with the mascarpone, soft butter, grated lemon peel and pepper.
steps.tip: Warm the bowl first with a little hot water so the sauce melts nicely.

steps: Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Tip the hot pasta into the bowl with a splash of pasta water and toss until creamy. Squeeze in a little lemon juice and scatter with dill.
steps.tip: No cooking for the salmon: the heat of the pasta is enough.

title: Linguine with zucchini, egg and parmesan
description: Thin strips of zucchini softened in olive oil and tossed with pasta and a silky egg and parmesan coating, like a summer carbonara. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil. Cut the zucchini into thin matchsticks and slice the onion thinly.

steps.text: Cook the onion and zucchini in the oil in a large pan on medium for 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Season with the salt.
steps.tip: Thin strips melt into the pasta, so every bite has some.

steps: Whisk 2 eggs and 2 yolks with the grated parmesan and the pepper.
Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Tip the pasta into the zucchini pan off the heat, pour in the egg mix and toss quickly with a splash of pasta water until creamy. Tear in the basil.
steps.tip: Off the heat, so the eggs make a silky sauce and do not scramble.

title: Pasta with prawns and zucchini
description: Zucchini sliced thin and grated, cooked in garlicky olive oil into a creamy sauce, with prawns added for the last two minutes. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil.

steps.text: Slice two zucchini into thin rounds and grate the third on the large holes of a grater.
steps.tip: Grated zucchini melts into a creamy sauce while the slices keep a bite.

steps: Warm the oil with the crushed garlic cloves in a large pan, add all the zucchini, the chili and salt and cook on medium for 10 minutes until soft. Remove the garlic.
Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Add the prawns to the zucchini and cook for 2 minutes until just pink.
steps.tip: Prawns go rubbery fast. Take them off as soon as they curl.

steps: Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water, a squeeze of lemon and the parsley, and serve.

title: Pasta e patate (Neapolitan pasta and potatoes)
description: Potatoes cooked down with onion, carrot and celery until they break up and make the sauce, with pasta cooked in and lots of parmesan. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Chop the onion, carrot and celeriac very finely. Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1 cm cubes.
Soften the vegetables in the oil in a deep pot for 8 minutes.

steps.text: Add the potatoes, bay leaves, salt and {1000 ml} water and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are soft and some start to fall apart.
steps.tip: A parmesan rind dropped in here adds lots of flavour, if you have one.

steps.text: Add the pasta and cook, stirring often, until soft, about 10 minutes. Add a little hot water if it gets too thick.
steps.tip: Stir well: the potato starch makes it creamy, but it can catch on the bottom.

steps: Off the heat, stir in most of the grated parmesan, the pepper and torn basil. Serve with the rest of the cheese.

title: Pasta with burst tomatoes and anchovy crumbs
description: Cherry tomatoes cooked in olive oil until they pop and make a juicy sauce, tossed with pasta and topped with crunchy anchovy breadcrumbs. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil.

steps.text: Warm {4 tbsp} of the oil with the crushed garlic cloves in a wide pan, add the whole cherry tomatoes, salt, oregano and chili. Cook on medium for 12 minutes, shaking the pan, until the skins burst and the juices thicken.
steps.tip: Press a few with a spoon to help them along.

steps.text: In a small pan, melt the chopped anchovies in the rest of the oil on low, add the breadcrumbs and toast for 4 minutes until golden and crunchy.
steps.tip: Keep stirring: breadcrumbs go from golden to burnt quickly.

steps: Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Toss the pasta with the tomatoes, torn basil and a splash of pasta water. Scatter the anchovy crumbs on top at the table.
steps.tip: Add the crumbs only at the last moment so they stay crunchy.

title: One-pot roast chicken with orzo and leek
description: Chicken legs browned and baked in a covered pot with leek, celery and white wine, then orzo stirred into the juices to finish. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Season the chicken with half the salt.

steps.text: Brown the chicken skin side down in the oil in a large ovenproof pot with a lid for 6 minutes until golden. Turn it over.
steps.tip: Golden skin now means flavour in the orzo later.

steps: Add the smashed garlic, chili, sliced leek, diced celeriac, half the parsley, the rest of the salt, the wine and {300 ml} water. Cover and bake for 50 minutes.

steps.text: Stir the orzo into the juices around the chicken with {300 ml} boiling water, cover and bake for 20 minutes more, until the orzo is soft and has soaked up the juices.
steps.tip: Check halfway and add a splash of water if it looks dry.

steps: Grate over the lemon peel, squeeze in some juice, scatter with the rest of the parsley and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
equipment: large ovenproof pot with a lid

title: Pasta alla genovese (onion and beef sauce)
description: Not pesto: the Neapolitan sauce of a kilo of onions and beef cooked slowly for two hours until the onions collapse into a sweet, glossy sauce. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Peel, halve and thinly slice the onions. Cut the beef into 2 cm pieces and the carrot into small cubes.

steps.text: Put the onions, beef, carrot, oil and salt into a heavy pot while it is still cold. Cover and cook on low for 1 hour, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: It looks like far too many onions. Trust it: they shrink to a quarter.

steps.text: Uncover and cook for another hour, adding a splash of wine every so often when it starts to stick, until the onions have melted into a thick, glossy, golden-brown sauce and the beef falls apart.
steps.tip: Low and slow. If it browns too fast, add a little water.

steps: Cook the pasta in salted water until just firm. Drain, keeping a little water.

steps.text: Toss the pasta with the sauce, a splash of pasta water, the pepper and most of the parmesan. Serve with the rest.
steps.tip: The sauce keeps 4 days and freezes well.

title: Cacio e pepe with Paški sir
description: The Roman three-ingredient pasta of sheep cheese, black pepper and pasta water whisked into a glossy sauce, made here with Croatian Paški sir. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.

ingredients.note: hard, such as Paški sir or pecorino

steps.text: Grate the cheese as finely as you can. Toast the pepper in a dry pan for 30 seconds until fragrant.
steps.tip: Very fine cheese melts smoothly. Coarse cheese makes clumps.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a smaller amount of lightly salted water than usual, so it gets extra starchy. Keep two cups of the water.
steps.tip: Go easy on the salt: the cheese is salty.

steps.text: In a big bowl, mix the cheese with a few spoons of the warm (not boiling) pasta water into a thick cream.
steps.tip: If the water is too hot the cheese goes stringy. Let it cool for a minute first.

steps: Drain the pasta, add it with the pepper to the bowl and toss fast, adding more pasta water a little at a time until glossy.
Serve at once with a green salad dressed with the oil and vinegar.

title: Lemon, parmesan and basil pasta
description: Pasta tossed with warm lemon butter, olive oil, lots of parmesan and fresh basil. Bright, fresh and ready in 15 minutes. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil.

steps.text: Grate the peel of both lemons and squeeze the juice of one. Warm the peel, juice, butter and oil in a large pan on low for 2 minutes until fragrant.
steps.tip: Just warm, never fry: you want the fresh lemon smell.

steps: Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Off the heat, toss the pasta in the lemon pan with the grated parmesan, the pepper and a splash of pasta water until creamy. Tear in the basil.
steps.tip: Add the cheese off the heat or it goes stringy. More lemon juice if you like it sharper.

title: Pasta with creamy walnut sauce
description: Walnuts blended with milk-soaked bread, garlic, parmesan and olive oil into an uncooked sauce from Liguria, loosened with pasta water. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil. Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Blend the walnuts, soaked bread, garlic, oregano, salt and half the parmesan, then blend in the oil into a thick cream.
steps.tip: Walnuts can taste bitter: pour boiling water over them for a minute and drain first if yours do.

steps: Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Toss the pasta with the walnut sauce and enough pasta water to make it coat smoothly. Serve with the rest of the parmesan.
steps.tip: The sauce is never cooked, so it keeps its fresh nutty taste. It keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Pasta with Sicilian tomato and almond pesto
description: A raw pesto from Trapani of tomatoes, almonds, basil and garlic blended with olive oil, tossed with hot pasta. A summer favourite. Inspired by An A-Z of Pasta by Rachel Roddy.
steps: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil.

steps.text: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 4 minutes until they smell nutty. Cool them a little.
steps.tip: Toasting deepens the flavour. Blanched almonds give a paler, creamier pesto.

steps.text: Blend the almonds with the garlic, basil, salt and pepper until coarse, then add the chopped tomatoes and the oil and pulse to a rough pesto.
steps.tip: Keep a little texture: it should not be a smooth purée.

steps: Cook the pasta until just firm. Keep a cup of the water and drain.

steps.text: Toss the hot pasta with the pesto and a splash of pasta water off the heat. Serve with grated parmesan.
steps.tip: Never cook this pesto: the heat of the pasta is enough.
